title: MFDB: a comprehensive database for marine fish functional genomics and evolutionary genomics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Site is live with no login. The genome download list (POST /download/getDonwload) returns species with GenBank/RefSeq assembly accessions and taxonomy strings. The RNA-seq download list returns 76 species. I downloaded the Atlantic cod expression file (GCF_902167405.1/rna, 23 MB): a tab-separated table of TPM (transcripts per million) values, 23,376 genes x 107 samples. Its column headers are free text and repeat ('Reference Station' x3, 'PFNA-C' x3, 'Cod gills', 'DMSO_1', SRR/ERR run IDs), and there is no tissue or condition metadata column. The sample-info endpoint (rna/getTranscripReuslt) failed with a server 'file does not exist' error for cod, salmon, fugu and leopard coral grouper. HEAD checks: cod annotation xlsx 28 MB, cod protein FASTA 15 MB, fugu RNA 8 MB, salmon RNA 200 MB.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 89 species, co-expression networks, core and pan gene sets, macrosynteny. These come from the abstract only; there is no full text (no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC).

a1_downloadable.note: Genome, GFF, CDS, protein, annotation and TPM files download without a login (checked the files directly).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No prediction target exists as a column. The expression matrices carry free-text, duplicated sample names and no tissue or condition field, and the sample-metadata endpoint is broken. Any tissue or condition label would have to be rebuilt from SRA/ENA (the public sequencing-read archives) run metadata across 76 species. Verified in the cod file.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein and coding sequences are downloadable as FASTA, so inputs are present.

a4_units_stated.note: Each sample's column has mean 42.78 over 23,376 genes, i.e. it sums to 1e6, which is consistent with TPM. The unit is implied by the endpoint path 'rna/tpm', not stated in the file.

a5_enough_rows.note: 23,376 genes in the cod matrix alone. Sample counts for the other species were not checked.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Salmon is the largest file seen (200 MB). Not every species was checked.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The abstract says 89 species and the RNA list has 76. That is plausible because not every species has RNA-seq data, but it was not reconciled against the full text.

a8_label_provenance.note: TPM values are reprocessed from public RNA-seq runs, so they are measurements, not model output. Annotations (GO/KEGG) are computational and would be circular as labels.

integration.partner_dataset: NCBI SRA/ENA run metadata (would be needed to rebuild tissue labels)
integration.join_key: SRR/ERR run accession (present only for some columns)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does protein sequence predict tissue-specific expression consistently across marine fish species?

honest_claim_h3: Not reachable: without per-sample tissue labels, no defined prediction target exists.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a gene's protein sequence to predict which tissues it is most active in, across many marine fish species.
plain_idea.train_on: Protein sequences of fish genes (23,376 genes in cod alone; other species unknown) with their measured activity across tissues.
plain_idea.predict: The tissue profile of each gene's activity, measured by RNA sequencing (reading out which genes are switched on in a sample). This needs tissue labels per sample, which the database does not provide.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Fish geneticists could annotate genes in poorly studied species. In practice the labels would first have to be rebuilt from archive metadata.

ml_idea: Predict tissue-specific expression from ESM-2 protein embeddings, holding out whole fish species. This is blocked: tissue labels per sample are absent, and the sample-info endpoint errors.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project failed at A2.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Call rna/getTranscripReuslt for any species. It returned a server error for all 4 tried, so no sample-to-tissue mapping is available.

verdict_reason: A2 fails. MFDB is a genome browser and download portal, not a labelled table. The expression matrices have free-text, duplicated sample names, no tissue or condition column, and the metadata endpoint is broken, so every label would have to be rebuilt from SRA/ENA across 76 species.
